name: Voyager 1
summary: A spacecraft that explored Jupiter and Saturn, then became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

status.label: Mission status needs review before publication

sections.title: Meet Voyager 1
sections.text: Voyager 1 is a robotic explorer. It carries cameras, science tools, a radio, and a Golden Record.

sections.title: Why did NASA send Voyager?
sections.text: Voyager 1 was sent to explore giant planets and their moons. Its discoveries helped people learn more about our solar system.

sections.title: How does it travel and talk?
sections.text: A big dish antenna sends radio signals. A long boom holds science tools away from the spacecraft. Radioisotope power sources make electricity far from the Sun.

sections.title: A journey beyond the Sun's bubble
sections.text: In 2012, NASA determined Voyager 1 had entered interstellar space, the space between stars. It keeps teaching us about the edge of our solar system.

sections.title: A Golden Message from Earth
sections.text: Voyager 1 carries a Golden Record with pictures, music, greetings, and natural sounds from Earth.

timeline.title: Voyager 1 launches
timeline.description: Voyager 1 begins its trip from Earth.

timeline.title: Voyager 1 explores Jupiter
timeline.description: It studies Jupiter and its moons, including active volcanoes on Io.

timeline.title: Voyager 1 explores Saturn
timeline.description: It sends observations of Saturn, its rings, and the moon Titan.

timeline.title: The Pale Blue Dot
timeline.description: Voyager 1 takes the images for a family portrait of the solar system, including tiny Earth.

timeline.title: Cameras rest
timeline.description: The cameras are turned off to save resources for the long journey.

timeline.title: Interstellar space
timeline.description: NASA determines that Voyager 1 enters the space between stars.

facts.title: Launched in 1977
facts.text: Voyager 1 began its journey on September 5, 1977.

facts.title: A hello from Earth
facts.text: It carries a Golden Record made to share a little about Earth and humanity.

facts.title: Tiny Earth
facts.text: Its Pale Blue Dot image shows Earth as a very small point of light.

activities.title: Meet Voyager 1
activities.description: Find out what kind of explorer Voyager is.
activities.objective: Know that Voyager 1 is a spacecraft.
activities.question: What is Voyager 1?
activities.explanation: Right! Voyager 1 is a robotic spacecraft that scientists use to explore space.

activities.title: Meet the Parts
activities.description: Choose the part that talks to Earth.
activities.question: Which part sends radio messages to Earth?
activities.hint: It is shaped a little like a giant bowl.
activities.explanation: Yes! The large dish antenna points toward Earth to send and receive radio signals.

activities.title: Blast Off
activities.description: Put the first part of Voyager's journey in order.
activities.objective: Understand that Voyager launched before visiting planets.
activities.question: What happened first?
activities.hint: A spacecraft has to leave Earth before it can visit another planet.
activities.explanation: Correct! Voyager 1 launched in 1977, before reaching Jupiter and later interstellar space.

activities.title: Where Did It Go?
activities.description: Choose a giant planet Voyager 1 explored.
activities.objective: Identify Jupiter as part of Voyager 1's journey.
activities.question: Which planet did Voyager 1 explore?
activities.hint: It is the largest planet in our solar system.
activities.explanation: Exactly! Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter in 1979 and learned about its moons.

activities.title: A Golden Message
activities.description: Discover what Voyager carries from Earth.
activities.objective: Know the purpose of the Golden Record.
activities.question: What is on Voyager's Golden Record?
answers: A map to a treasure chest
activities.hint: It is a message that shares things from Earth.
activities.explanation: Yes! The Golden Record carries a collection of sounds, images, music, and greetings from Earth.
